text: A bike’s braking system is built to brake a rider from the inside out, from the road to the pavement to the tire. It begins with a solid-state brake that absorbs energy from the rider’s effort. This brake has a built-in air reservoir to help stop the bike from spinning out of control. Next, a small fan keeps the brake in place with air pressure to help the rider keep control of the bike. The rider’s speed is controlled by a belt with a clutch mechanism. Finally, the brake, the fan and the clutch are all controlled by a hand brake, which is designed to stop a moving bike by applying a constant force to the brake pedal.
